recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source correction is needed for FHIR-25471; future timing-choice changes should proceed through later timing trackers rather than reintroducing static dateTime or Period choices.
issue_request: FHIR-25471 asked to remove dateTime and Period from ActivityDefinition timing choices because static dateTime and Period values do not make sense in a definitional resource, and to clarify that timing is evaluated during apply to populate resulting request actions.
initial_application: Commit 1b8c8728485bc9bfa8dcc454047dba518eca81e5 explicitly applied J#25471 by removing dateTime and Period from ActivityDefinition.timing[x] and the parallel PlanDefinition.action.timing[x], and by adding the explanatory apply-operation timing comments.
additional_context: ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition are active approved current-build resources. Later timing-family work, including FHIR-29799 clarification and FHIR-43696 adding RelativeTime, refined the same elements without reintroducing dateTime or Period.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the authoritative current StructureDefinition source for ActivityDefinition.timing[x] allows Timing, Age, Range, Duration, and RelativeTime, but not dateTime or Period, and its comment explains apply-time interpretation. The parallel PlanDefinition.action.timing[x] source remains consistent.

related_jiras.note: Requested explanation of definitional timing choices and was satisfied by the same explanatory comments initially added with FHIR-25471, then reconciled later for RelativeTime.
